Meet gorgeous Bruce!  Bruce has had a very difficult start in life.  When he first came into our care, he was in a truly sorry state.  He was extremely thin, and his skin was in a terrible condition.  His body was bald, red and very inflamed, and it was clear that he had not had the care he desperately needed.  After lots of veterinary visits, treatment, time and plenty of TLC, we are so pleased to see the changes in him.  His fur is beginning to grow back, he is gaining weight, and he is slowly starting to feel better in himself.  Bruce is a very frightened and timid boy.  The world is a scary place for him, and he can be extremely nervous and shut down.  He will need someone who understands that building his confidence will not happen overnight.  However, once Bruce learns to trust you, you see a completely different side to him.  He is a very affectionate, playful and loving boy who enjoys being close to the people he feels safe with.  Bruce will need lots of time, patience, understanding and reassurance.  His new adopter must be prepared to give him the space he needs and allow him to progress at his own pace.  This could take some considerable time, and there may be setbacks along the way.  He is looking for an experienced owner who has previous experience with very nervous and fearful dogs and understands the commitment involved in helping a dog like Bruce learn that the world can be a safe place.  Bruce has already come such a long way, and we believe there is a wonderful, affectionate boy waiting to emerge as his confidence grows.  He deserves a quiet, patient and loving home where he can finally feel safe, secure and cherished.  The potential adopter must commit to multiple regular meet and greets for Bruce to get to know then before the adoption can take place.  He will need a private secure garden.

Bruce has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, he can be ok with some and very unsure around others, so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he can get 100% of the love and attention.

As Bruce is so timid we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Maggie
description:
Meet Maggie!  Maggie is a friendly, affectionate girl who absolutely loves being around people.  She enjoys nothing more than a good fuss and, if you’re offering belly scratches she’ll be your best friend!  Maggie has recently had BOAS surgery with us and has recovered brilliantly,  She is already feeling much better, and it’s wonderful to see her enjoying life with improved comfort and breathing.  She is now ready to find a loving family who will continue to give her all the care, attention and affection she deserves.  Maggie is a gorgeous girl with plenty of love to give, and we’re looking forward to seeing her find the special home she has been waiting for.

Maggie has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel following a successful meet and greet she could potentially live with another dog of similar size.

As Maggie came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mischief
description:
Meet Mischief!  This lovely girl is looking for a very special home.  Mischief is a very timid and nervous girl who has slowly started to come out of her shell.  She will need patient, understanding adopters who are willing to give her the time and space she needs to build confidence and learn that she is safe.  Once Mischief trusts you, you get to see the sweet girl underneath.  She is affectionate and loving, enjoys giving kisses, and absolutely loves a good belly rub.  Seeing her begin to relax and show her gentle personality is incredibly rewarding.  Mischief does have a cheeky side to her name!  She is a talented escape artist and has been known to jump the kennel walls, so her new home will need secure fencing and adopters who are prepared for her Houdini tendencies.  Extra care will be needed to make sure the doesn’t escape open doors or fences.  Mischief is not looking for a busy or rushed home.  She needs someone who understands that trust takes time and is willing to let her progress at her own pace.  Any potential adopters will need to commit to several regular meet and greets before the adoption can take place.

Mischief has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, although she does prefer a calmer dog.  We do feel she could be rehomed with another calm dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Mischief came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be very nervous we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Bear
description:
Bear is a very nervous boy when he meets new people for the first time. It takes a little while for him to come around but with patience and yummy treats he slowly starts to trust you. Once he has gained your trust and is comfortable he is an affectionate boy and loves to give out kisses. He will need to have multiple regular meets before going home.

Bear is a big dog who doesn’t understand his size, he is constantly jumping up for cuddles and doesn’t know what personal space is. Bear is going to require a lot of training to help him learn manners. He can be a very cheeky boy at times! He will need socialising in different environments and around people to help him build his confidence up. Bear gets super excited when going for walks and is very strong on the lead, this is another area that will need more training. Bear loves playing with his toys, splashing around in water and zooming around our enclosed area.

Bear is after an adult only home that has previous experience with big boisterous dogs. No regular visiting children either please. He is going to need a very active home with a family that is able to provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep him busy. As he is still only a young dog he can get up to mischief when he is bored. Bear’s new family need to be committed to putting in the training that he needs not only initially but keeping it up for the rest of his life.

Bear needs to be the only dog in the home so that he can have all of attention to help get him settled. Bear can interact well with dogs whilst out on walks but will need further training to help improve this.

We know that Bear is going to require a lot of work at first but once he is trained he will make a lovely family dog who will love going on plenty of adventures. Taking on a dog this size is a big commitment, please ensure that you are serious and have thought about the future before applying.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an ex-racing greyhound that has spent all of his life in kennels. Jasper is now ready for a comfortable and cosy forever home to call his own. Jasper is a friendly and loveable boy who likes attention and a cuddle. Jasper has a high prey drive still so does pull when he sees ducks, birds and wildlife when out on walks. Jasper has never lived in a home before so he will need time to settle and get used to unfamiliar sounds and objects.

Jasper has interacted well with dogs and is currently paired with another greyhound so we believe that he can be rehomed with another dog of a similar size – Subject to a successful meet.

Jasper is a sweet boy so can potentially be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Jax
description:
This stunning boy is Jax! we are looking for an experienced home for this fantastic lad.  He is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!  As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

Jax was rehomed but sadly has been returned to us as his prey drive was too much for his new owners. He cannot be rehomed with cats or small furries.  He will need an owner that has previous experience with large breed high prey dogs.

He has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could possibly be rehomed with another dog (similar size) following a successful meet and greet.

As Jax came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a very loveable boy who just wants to give out hugs to everyone he meets, he does sometimes forget how big he is though. He’s a big hit with volunteers here and they all love taking him out for his walks as they get to have lots of cuddles. He can be strong on the lead though due to his size. He’s a very sweet boy who has a big heart and is looking for someone to show him lots of love! Sam has enjoyed his walks around the woods, watching the ducks and wildlife around him. Sam would appreciate an enclosed garden that he can spend his time in relaxing and enjoying the sun. Sam loves his treats, nothing is too big or small for him – he isn’t fussy!

Sam is super friendly with everyone he meets but due to his giddy jumpy nature we believe that it would be best to rehome Sam with children over the age of 16 – subject to a successful meet and greet.

Sam needs to be the only dog in the home, he can be vocal around dogs so needs a family that has experience to help build his confidence and manners.

If you think that you could provide a comfortable home with lots of treats for Sam please apply now!

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, which was over 200 days now! It has taken a lot of time for staff and volunteers to get to know Cali and bring out her excitable, bubbly personality. Cali loves going for walks and off lead runs in our compound area, she will always be found with a football in her mouth. She loves to dodge past you whilst you try and catch her, her tail never stops wagging. Cali loves her treats and sits nicely whilst you give them to her. She has been toilet trained whilst in our care, which is a bonus for when she goes home.

Cali can be strong on the lead at times due to her excitement to get outside and enjoy the fresh air but can walk nicely after her initial excitement is over, especially on a harness. Cali would love a fully enclosed garden with someone around most of the time so that she can come and go as she pleases. Cali spends most of her day relaxing on a comfy bed watching people come and go. She can be a little barky in her kennel at first but this is due to her wanting to say hello to everyone.

Cali isn’t a cuddly kind of girl but would love a family that is willing to keep her entertained and will play with her toys. We believe that Cali needs to be in an adult only home, with a family that has experience with rescue dogs or bull breeds.

Cali was nervous of dogs when she first came into our care so we think that it is best that she is the only dog in the house. With a lot of socialisation she now is a friendly girl that is happy to say hello to most dogs that she meets.

We think that it would be best for Cali to not be in a house with cats.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Tails
description:
This stunning girl is Tails.  We are looking for a committed and knowledgeable home for her where she can truly thrive.  As a typical Husky she is full of energy and very intelligent so will need an owner who understands the unique needs of this incredible breed. She is very high energy and an independent thinker with a typical Husky stubborn streak. She will need a home that has an active lifestyle where she can have plenty of exercise, enrichment and ongoing training.  Tails has so much potential and will make a loyal, fun and rewarding companion in the right home.  We are looking for someone patient, understanding and ready to invest time into building a strong bond with her.

Tails has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

As Tails came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her, so we think it would be best for her to go to an adult only home.

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Paddy
description:
Paddy is a confident, happy Dachshund looking for a new home to call his own. He is 4 years old and has come to us through no fault of his own ans is currently in one of our wonderful foster homes. Paddy could be an only dog or live with another dog in his new family and could live with older primary school children and above.

Paddy is a wonderful little boy who loves treats and being out and about, he has always lived with another dog and got on great but could be the only dog in his new home if he wasn't going to be left home alone for too long and he has also lived with a toddler and done great, however in a new home we would want any new children to be of older primary school aged. Paddy travels well in the car, loves a cuddle and has met multiple dogs here with no issues, he is a wonderful dog all round and is going to make the most fun loving addition to a lucky new family.

name: Alfie
description:
Alfie is looking for an active home who want to teach him some fun skills and put his brain to use. He prefers the company of humans, so much so, that he would prefer to to be the only pet in the home. Alfie mostly will ignore dogs out and about, especially if you have a ball for a distraction. Alfie likes to keep things that he finds on the floor and may resist handing them over over, so an older teen -adult home would be more suitable for him in these situations. Alfie likes to sleep in a cosy crate den overnight as he finds this comforting and is he is fully housetrained. Alfie travels well in the car, he just needs a little helping hand getting in. Alfie's adopters will need to commit to helping him on his weight loss journey, so that he can fully enjoy going on adventures!

Alfie thrives when he is outdoors and playing with his ball and will be perfect for an active household. He can live with children of late teenage and upwards who will also follow the advice given when Alfie does pick up items he shouldn't have and understand not to take things directly off him. Further training is essential for Alfie, so if you feel you have the time and patience to help Alfie move forward in his new journey, then please click that favourite button! He will be worth the effort.

name: Penny
description:
Penny is a super sweet 8 year old Cocker Spaniel looking for a loving new home to call her own after coming into our care through no fault of her own. Penny is looking for a new home where there is ideally another kind dog in the home for company and confidence, however in the right home she could be an only dog. Penny would like new humans who enjoy the company of a super sweet, very affectionate dog who would like to snuggle up and have human contact on the sofa and basically be your side kick! She could live with older primary aged children and above.

Penny is absolutley adorable and will no doubt make you fall in love! She adores tasty treats and loves to explore and run around with the other dogs. Penny loves us humans a lot and would like to be able to snuggle on the sofa and be with her humans ging in their daily lives, she is going to make some family very lucky!

name: Rocky
description:
Lexi and Rocky are looking for a home where they will be the only pets but can live with secondary school aged children. They are very close so need to live together. Leaving hours can be built up to 4-5 once settled. They would prefer a quieter home environment.

Lexi and Rocky are best friends and are looking for a loving family to extend their friendship circle. They are clever, keen and very caring. They will enjoy access to quieter walks and love to learn for a tasty treat. If you are looking to add two, smaller best friends to your home then Rocky and Lexi just might be the perfect pair.

name: Lexi
description:
Lexi and Rocky are looking for a home where they will be the only pets but can live with secondary school aged children. They are very close so need to live together. Leaving hours can be built up to 4-5 once settled. They would prefer a quieter home environment.

Lexi and Rocky are best friends and are looking for a loving family to extend their friendship circle. They are clever, keen and very caring. They will enjoy access to quieter walks and love to learn for a tasty treat. If you are looking to add two, smaller best friends to your home then Rocky and Lexi just might be the perfect pair.

name: Hustle
description:
Super fun pocket rocket Hustle is a 1 year old Staffordshire Bull Terrier who gives everything 110% and has a real lust for life. He loves to use his brain and is the happiest chappie you will meet. He likes playtime and enjoys fetch with a tennis ball; he will zoom around after anything thrown for him or a good game with a flirt pole. Once he has burnt off some energy, he is eager for a fuss, he will paw you or climb into your lap and give you lots of kisses all over your face. Looking for a new adventures buddy, then Hustle is your guy!

Hustle is looking for a home with loving and active adopters who can take him on sniffy adventures, who will take the time to help him settle in and give him all the love and attention he deserves. He is a sweet boy who can live with older secondary school children who are confident around bouncy and playful dogs, who will understand that can be a little clumsy when excited, who will play with him nicely and will give him space to rest when needed. Hustle can be a little frustrated around other dogs and can be a little over the top so would prefer to be the only dog in the home, he would however be happy with polite and friendly walking buddies. Hustle is a clever but busy boy, once he has had a good play he could engage in training in short, sweet sessions as long as a tasty treat is on offer. Hustle would like his own private, secure garden where he can spend play time so he can burn off some energy. He does tend to worry when left so is looking for someone home the majority of the time, especially to begin with, any leaving time would need to be built up slowly once he has had time to settle into his new home. Hustle will need to meet his adopters a few times prior to going home so please bear all of this in mind when applying.

name: Nuche
description:
Looking for a super smart, super fun and super handsome Lurcher? Then meet Nuche! He’s 3yrs old and bursting with potential. He’s quite shy initially but once he’s familiar there’s no stopping him! He’s very affectionate and loves to snuggle with his friends. He’s also really playful. If you bring the toys out, you’ll make his day! He’s fine to make doggy friends out and about for walkies but doesn’t like to share his home so will need to be the only pet. He needs a calm home and a consistent routine, so an adult only home would be ideal. He’s already house trained too!

Nuche has a lot going for him. He’s very clever and already learned lots of useful cues, and being very foody he’s always keen to learn more. He travels well in a car so will enjoy joining his new family on outdoors adventures in peaceful places. He happily wears his muzzle out and about as he does have a habit of picking things up he shouldn’t! His favourite places to explore are beaches, woods and rivers as he does love the water! So if you are looking for an exceptionally fun and interactive young dog and you have time to work with us to settle him in slowly, add Nuche to your favourites now!

name: Jupiter
description:
Are you looking for THE most loyal and loving BFF and are up for learning some great dog training along the way? Then meet Jupiter! He’s a 7yr old Dobermann Cross who forms a very strong bond with his friends. Jupiter loves to cuddle and be by your side! He likes to be with his friends so it will be a little while until he can be built up to any time on his own, but this just means more Jupiter cuddles!! He’s spent a lot of time on sleepovers with his favourite handlers and proven that he’s fully housetrained, really playful (tennis balls are his favourite!) and the best sofa snuggler you could wish for! So, if you are looking for an AWESOME dog who will be a little bit of a project initially but will then repay you with a lifetime of love and fun, add Jupiter to your favourites NOW!

Jupiter can be a bit anxious with new people and places so will need his adopters to slowly work with us to build a bond and prepare him for life in his forever home. He’s worried by other dogs so is best walked in quiet places where he won’t see many, but he happily wears his muzzle. He’s made good progress with his training and has even made a couple of doggy friends at the centre, so in time walking buddies should be possible if introduced properly. He needs a calm and predictable adult only home where he can build a good routine and continue smashing his training. He will need to have his own secure garden with high fence as he loves to play off-lead.

name: Morticia
description:
Morticia and her brothers are looking for their forever homes separately. They are 10 week old Staffordshire Bull Terrier crossbreed pups who are full of energy and fun! We believe they will grow to medium size and they will require all forms of puppy training from toilet training, lead walking, socialisation and much more. Morticia and siblings can live with other pets and dog savvy children.

Morticia and brothers will require lots of training, enrichment and appropriate exercise through out their life. As they are so young they will need a fully secure garden and a family with short leaving hours to help them settle in to living in a home. These pups are full of fun and mischief and ready to grow and learn in their new home. If you have time and patience and are ready to welcome a new addition to your family, just fill in an application, and don't forget to 'Favourite' them!

name: Lexi
description:
Lexi is a gorgeous 8yr old Pug who is looking for a peaceful home to snuggle on the sofa with her new family. She has been getting over a couple of medical ailments but is very much recovered now and ready to find her forever home. She'll be fine with older kids who understand that she likes a peaceful life. She is fine around other dogs and could potentially share her home with a similar chilled older dog like herself as long as they get on well together.

Lexi is a real sweetheart and enjoys nothing more than snuggling up with her human friends. She is super friendly with everyone she meets. She is currently living off-site in a foster home and her carer tells us she is wonderful company. Almost fully house trained, fine to be left for a couple of hours on her own and very easy to walk on lead. Add Lexi to your favourites if you're looking for a little lady to shower you in love and affection.

name: Mike
description:
Marvellous Mike really lives up to his nickname and is a such a sweetheart. He's come into our care with little known about his past so will need a patient family who are prepared to teach him all he needs to know about life in a home. Mike is a lovely boy who is affectionate with his favourite people. He can be a little worried at times especially with new and novel things, like cars, so will need some support and guidance as he figures things out. Mike could share his home with another dog (or dogs) and could live with lower primary aged children following a meeting here at the centre. Mike is a sweet boy who really enjoys his walkies, so he would thrive with an active and fun loving family who would like a new best friend for every adventure! He may need some support as he settles in to his forever home, including help with things like housetrained and learning how to settle and relax home alone. We recommend any time being left is built up gradually as he settles in.

Mike is a really sweet lad, who enjoys being with people. Being a harrier hound, Mike is an active boy who enjoys following his nose. His new family will need to prepare for some houndy mischief as his personality shines through and be committed to helping his positively channel his taste for adventure! Sully is a wonderful boy, but does have some medical needs which means he is partially sighted. He's not currently on any medication for this and he doesn't let this hold him back but his new family should be aware for any future needs.

name: Bruno
description:
Bruno is a gorgeous 2-year-old Dogue de Bordeaux/Rottweiler cross who is looking for a home where he can be the only pet, although he could have some doggy walking friends. He can live with primary school-aged children and can be left for up to 4 hours. Bruno also travels well in the car and would love a home where he can enjoy plenty of love, lots of fun and, most importantly, a comfy sofa to call his own!

Bruno is a real-life BFG — he may be a little shy when you first meet him, but once he knows you, he is the biggest softie with an enormous heart. He absolutely loves his home comforts and would happily curl up on the sofa with you. Despite his size, Bruno is convinced he is a lap dog and thoroughly enjoys a good cuddle! He also loves playing with a ball and having a fun game of tug with his soft toys.

name: Rae
description:
Rae is a lovely 7-year-old Springer Spaniel who can live happily with other dogs and children of any age. She can be left for  up to 4 hrs and travels really well in the car. Where is my husband? More like, where is my home?

Rae is the sweetest angel girl with a calm, gentle and incredibly loving nature. She has the loveliest face and a personality that will make anyone smile. She adores her tennis ball and loves searching for and chasing it, but she is just as happy enjoying cuddles and being close to her people.

name: Mia
description:
Sweet and gentle girl Mia is a 7 year old Boxer cross who loves to prove how clever she is by showing off her cool tricks. One of her favourite pastimes is to sniff and explore in open green spaces where she can relax and take it all in at her leisure. Playtime is the best, she will jump and chase around after her toys, sometimes taking time out to de-fluff a teddy or two, but the best way to this girl’s heart is a tennis ball or 2 (or 3). She is a snuggly lady, she likes neck scratches the most and will paw you if you stop too soon. This gorgeous girl would make the perfect addition to any family home seeking a snuggle bug of a dog!

Mia is looking for a calm home with loving adopters who can take her on gentle, sniffy strolls away from busy, built up areas where she can relax and explore at her leisure. She is a friendly girl who can live with older secondary school children who will let her approach at her leisure, who can play with her nicely and will give her space to rest when needed. Mia often chooses to avoid other dogs when out and about, so would prefer to be the only dog in the home, but could meet up with polite and friendly walking buddies. Mia has plenty training under her belt, she does a lovely “sit”, “paw” and “down”, as well as “leave it,” “bed,” and “come” – impressive right?! She would be eager to engage in training if a tasty treat is on offer, and is proof that an older dog can learn new tricks, she is currently being muzzle trained as she will need to be on a lead and muzzle at all times in public. She would like a home with a private, secure garden for her to potter about in at her leisure and have some quality off lead time. Mia can be worried by being left so is looking for a family with someone home the majority of the time. Any leaving time would need to be built up slowly once she has had time to settle into her new home. Mia will need to meet her adopters a few times prior to going home so please bear this in mind when applying.

name: Winnie
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and have a previous eye ulcer.

12-08-26 Winnie is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She has clearly had some very difficult experiences in her past, and at the moment she finds it incredibly hard to trust people or believe that we mean her no harm. She is an extremely frightened little girl who needs a very special and experienced home where she can begin to learn that life can be safe and that human hands can be kind.

Winnie is currently finding human interaction and handling exceptionally overwhelming. If someone approaches her too closely, she can become extremely distressed and will bark continuously as she panics. Being picked up is particularly frightening for her, and when she feels trapped or unable to escape, she will bite wherever she can reach. She may also toilet through fear when someone attempts to pick her up. These behaviours are coming from a place of extreme fear and a desperate attempt to protect herself, but they are very real behaviours that her adopters will need to understand and be prepared to manage safely. Winnie is not currently a dog who can be handled casually, and her future family will need to be very experienced with severely frightened ex-breeding dogs and confident in reading her body language and respecting her boundaries.

Winnie will need a very calm and quiet, adult-only home with no pressure placed upon her to interact before she is ready. Her adopters will need to understand that building a relationship with Winnie is likely to be a long journey, and progress may be very gradual. She will need people who are willing to allow her to take things completely at her own pace, while providing a safe, predictable environment where she can slowly learn that she is not going to be hurt.

Despite how frightened Winnie is of people, she is already showing us some lovely glimpses of the little dog underneath her fears. She absolutely loves toys and food, and although she isn't yet brave enough to take treats directly from our hands, she is more than happy to join in with treat time when treats are gently thrown towards her. She is also beginning to enjoy the simple comfort of being cosy in a big, comfy duvet. These small things are incredibly important for Winnie and give us hope that, as she begins to feel safer, we will see more and more of her personality emerge.

Winnie will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance and companionship. Having another dog around may help her feel safer and give her a familiar canine friend to follow as she learns about her new life. Her adopters will need to ensure that any resident dog is calm, confident and able to give Winnie the space she needs.

Winnie has never lived in a home before, so absolutely everything will be new to her. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life, including house training and the everyday sights and sounds of a household. Lead walking is not something Winnie is ready for at this stage, and her new home will need a very secure garden where she can begin to explore safely without being overwhelmed.

Winnie is not going to be an easy dog, and she will require a significant level of commitment, experience and patience from her adopters. However, she is not a lost cause. She is a deeply frightened little girl who has not yet had the opportunity to understand that people can be trusted. Seeing a dog like Winnie slowly begin to feel safe and choose to engage with the people around her can be incredibly rewarding, but her adopters must be prepared for this to take time.

Winnie needs someone truly special who understands just how serious her fears are and is willing to give her the space, security and patience she needs. Beneath all that fear is a little girl who loves food, adores toys and is beginning to discover the comfort of a cosy bed. With the right experienced home and plenty of time, we hope Winnie will one day feel safe enough to let her true personality shine.

Will arrived with an old eye ulcer that has healed. Our vets have assessed this and are not concerned at the moment but it will need monitoring as if it does start to cause her pain it may need removal in the future, which would not be covered by insurance.

Winnie has been given the Gift of Life by Jo Rowlands

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

name: Geneva
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

29-08-26 Geneva has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is feeling quite overwhelmed by all the changes in her world and is going to need lots of love, patience and TLC from her new family. Geneva isn't used to being handled and it is clear that she hasn't had much socialisation in her life so far. She finds being picked up and handled quite worrying, but once she is safely in your arms she does settle and seems to enjoy having a gentle stroke. She is a sweet girl who just needs someone to show her that people can be kind and that the world isn't such a scary place.

Geneva will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need to settle in at her own pace. We would consider a home with teenagers aged 16+ who are calm and respectful around dogs.

Geneva will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the ropes and take her under their wing. Having a canine friend will be very important for her as she learns that home life can be a safe and happy place.

Geneva has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness, so she will need to practise wearing these around the home and garden first, gradually building her confidence before she is ready to venture further afield. Her new family will need to take things at her pace and understand that progress may be slow to begin with.

Geneva is a sweet little soul who has so much to learn, but with the right home, a kind resident dog and patient adopters, we hope she will blossom into a happy and confident little companion. She needs someone who will see the frightened girl she is today and be willing to give her the time and love she needs to discover just how wonderful life can be.

Geneva arrived with us showing signs of a urine infection and possible bladder stones. She has been treated for the urine infection and has had multiple small bladder stones removed.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with one kind resident dog. I cannot live with cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk well on a lead and harness, and am doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Gail has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived with us she was a very scared girl who found human interaction extremely overwhelming and would often hide away at the back of her kennel. It was clear that she hadn't had much socialisation before and was in desperate need of love and TLC. Since then Gail has started to come out of her shell and has made really encouraging progress. Although she is still a very nervous girl, once she gets to know you she does start to come out of her shell and will approach you for a gentle sniff and will allow you to gently stroke her, although still finds this very worrying.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to come out of her shell and settle in at her own pace. Gail is a sensitive little girl and does really struggle with change, so she is likely to go backwards in her new home at first and will need time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Gail does rely on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will be looking for a home where there is just one other kind, confident resident dog to be her friend. Gail doesn't really enjoy sharing her space with more than one dog and can be a little sassy and has shown that she much prefers just having one other dog to make her best friend. She does take a little while to warm up to other dogs, but once she bonds with them she absolutely adores them and finds confidence from them.

Gail has learned all about walking on a lead and harness since arriving with us and as long as she has a doggy friend by her side, now even goes for walks with some of our volunteers, which is very brave of her! She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

Shortly after Gail's arrival to us, she started showing signs of back pain as well as some weakness and unsteadiness. As she's a dachshund and they can be quite prone to spinal issues, she went for x-rays to be on the safe side. The x-rays showed several mineralised discs in her spine, but did not show any obvious spinal cord compression. She was given pain relief and was put on crate rest, and initially returned to activity with the help of a supportive back brace. Gail has made a good recovery and is currently doing very well.

Gail's adopters will need to be aware that should she have any further issues in the future related to this, it would be classed as a pre-existing condition and would not be covered by insurance.

Gail is a truly special little girl who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She is still a very scared girl, and although her journey may not be a quick one, with lots of love, patience and TLC, we know it will be incredibly rewarding to watch her grow in confidence and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

What incredible progress this girl is making! I'm constantly impressed and surprised by her.I only work with Gail 1-2 times a month, and I'm always blown away by how far she's come when I see her again. Some things that may not seem like much can be huge milestones for our ex-breeding dogs - three months ago, Gail could only be touched by a few members of staff and was very anxious in human presence; six weeks ago, she would only tolerate having her harness put on and being walked by the two people she knew best; two weeks ago, she was walking with a few people but still spending most of her time in the back of her kennel hiding, and would try to hide in corners if she saw anyone unfamiliar; and today, she went on a 20 minute walk with me, then cuddled in my lap afterwards! She even goes for walks with volunteers she's never met before and is incredibly brave meeting new people. When visitors walk past, Gail runs to the front of her kennel with her tail wagging.Gail is a lovely little dog with so much personality. She's going to be the queen of wherever she ends up, and she deserves to be spoiled rotten! Hopefully, Gail's perfect home is right around the corner. Until then, we'll keep on showing her all the love and kindness we can.

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

name: Hachi
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with another kind dog. I am fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead, but it's still very new for me.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

19-09-26 Hachi is a super sweet old man who has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He has been through so much and is now looking for the perfect retirement home where he can enjoy his golden years surrounded by love, comfort and plenty of cosy naps.

When Hachi first arrived with us, he was sadly very unwell and was passing a lot of blood in his urine and needing to urinate constantly. He required emergency surgery, during which a large 3cm bladder stone was discovered. This must have been causing him a great deal of pain and discomfort, but thankfully the stone was removed and Hachi has made a wonderful recovery. He also had two teeth extracted at the same time and has been treated for a ear infection.

Hachi has been in foster with a member of staff since arriving with us so that he could recover in a quiet and comfortable environment. He is an incredibly sweet and loving boy who adores fuss and attention and loves to give paw! He spends a lot of his time sleeping, but as his recovery has continued, he has definitely found a little spring in his step. His playful side is starting to emerge too, which is absolutely adorable, and he is even beginning to discover the joys of playing with toys!

Hachi is a fairly confident boy and is very people focused, but he also really enjoys the company of other dogs. He loves snuggling up with his doggy friends, so would be very happy to have another kind and friendly resident dog in his new home to keep him company. In the right circumstances and with adopters who are around most of the time, we would consider homing him as an only dog. He will be looking for an adult only home, as we feel he would prefer a quiet and peaceful retirement home, but he has met young children well and would be fine to have visiting children around. He has also meet a cat fine and so could possibly be homed with a dog savvy cat.

Hachi had never lived in a home before moving into foster, so he has had lots to learn, but he is doing brilliantly and is really enjoying discovering what home life is all about. He is doing well with his house training, although he will need kind and patient adopters who understand that he is still learning. He has been wearing nappies around the house while he has been recovering from his surgery as at the moment he can leak a bit, which is to be expected and these don't seem to bother him at all.

Hachi is beginning to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and is doing really well. We think he will enjoy gentle little adventures with his new family, followed by curling up in a comfy bed and having a well earned nap.

Hachi has been through so much, but he has remained the sweetest boy throughout it all. Now that he is feeling so much better, we would love to find him a special retirement home where he can be cherished, pampered and allowed to enjoy all the simple pleasures of life.

He hasn't been castrated as our vet felt like this would be too much to put him through on top of the other surgeries, so his adopters will need to sign a disclaimer to ensure they understand this and that he cannot be around unspayed female dogs.

Hachi has been given the Gift of Life by Jade Mitchell

name: KoKo
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a mammary lump that will be assessed during my spay.

04-10-26 KoKo is a nervous lady who has come to us from a breeder and is trying so hard to be brave. She does get excited when she sees you and is starting to show more of her lovely personality, but she can still be on the shy side and will need time and patience to continue building her confidence. She does allow you to gently stroke her and seems to quite enjoy this!

KoKo will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and allow her to lean on them as she settles in.
