These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Crumble
description:
I need an adult-only, experienced home where I can feel safe and loved.

I want to be the only dog in the house. No cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Crumble is a lovely lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings. She seems to be gaining confidence each day, which is wonderful to see.

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where she can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

On arrival, our vets noted that Crumble had a Grade 2 luxating patella. During her time with us she has shown very intermittent lameness, mostly only seen when she’s getting up from laying down for a long time. She was sent for x-rays which showed potential damage to her left cruciate ligament, as well as hip dysplasia in her right hip. She is currently managing very well with rest and pain relief, and we will work on building correct muscle tone to support her as well as slow introductions to controlled exercise and physio.

Crumble is the most incredible girl who loves her humans once she has bonded with you. She has such a huge personality and makes all of her kennel mums and dads laugh every single day.

She absolutely loves playing with her best friend Criss Cross and she loves splashing in water when it's warm weather.

She's one of those exceptional girls who will make someone incredibly lucky and give them so much love and fun once they've put in the time to earn her trust and build that bond with her.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.

He will need a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence at his own pace. He also appreciates having a quiet space at mealtimes where he feels safe and secure. Criss Cross will need a home without cats as he is overly interested in them.

Criss Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet-natured gentle giant with so much love to give. With patience, understanding, endless bum scratches and plenty of tasty treats, he has every chance to flourish into the loyal and devoted companion he is meant to be.

Criss Crosswill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Criss Cross has been doing very well socialising with other dogs, he walks politely next to calm dogs and even had a muzzled play date the other day. His best friend Crumble is currently on kennel rest, so he only gets to see her very briefly whilst on lead, but he always runs to the front of her kennel to say hello before going back to his own kennel.

He is such a sweet boy who adores his people once he trusts you. He just needs positive introductions to feel comfortable with new people. Very proud of the progress he's been making and we'll continue to work on his doggy social skills.

Criss Cross is such a sweetheart! He is loyal to his friend Crumble, his kennel mums and dads. He’s still greeting everyone on walks with a bit of caution but once he’s recognised you, you’re considered family.

He’s going on occasional independent walks to gain his confidence but he is always looking for Crumble to keep him company. He’s very cautious of new things however day by day his confidence is growing and with his trust in his kennel mums he always runs back to check they’re okay, showing you just how brave he is and continues to be, so when the right home finds him….they will have to earn his trust and give him the patience and love he truly deserves.

This distinguished gent is progressing so well, every day!

He has started to get in the practice of being kennel clean, one of his kennel mums likes to come in a little early to help him practice this so when he finds his forever home it might be a little less stressful learning toilet training skills properly.

Criss Cross is even getting more adventurous greeting people on his daily walks now just to  say hello and maybe scoring a treat or fuss, and even recognising some of the staff when they visit him.

He is protective of Crumble and always looks to see her catching up on their daily walks, and enjoys playing with her or being near watching over her. But when he has his solo kennel time, he has been exploring his personal toy collection, anything with a treat in it and he’s happy. This cuddle bug deserves a home with endless bum scratches and scrumptious treats

This handsome guy is progressing every day! And showing his kennel mums just how much of a sweetheart he is. He is an affectionate goofball once he’s comfortable with you. He enjoys playing with his chow friend Crumble and he loves getting love from her and his kennel mums. He loves to jump up to have his harness put on, refusing to stand still because he gets so excited to go out and explore with Crumble.

Criss Cross will now even allow some of his part time kennel mums and dads to give him attention too. He is still very cautious of new people but is slowly meeting new people and remembering them!

With some time his new family will find out just how special Criss Cross is!

Criss Cross has made incredible progress over the last few days. He used to hide and grumble when people approached his kennel, but this has changed massively!

Now, Criss Cross comes up to the kennel door and wags his tail, getting very excited to see people. Spending time with this handsome boy brings me so much joy; I often find myself straying from my section just to sneak in five minutes of cuddles.

Criss Cross is still looking for a quiet, gentle home and someone who will take things slow while he gets to know them.

Criss-Cross has grown into an incredibly sociable and interactive boy, although he can still be a little shy when first meeting new people. Once he feels comfortable, he actively seeks out attention and loves a cuddle, often trying to give kisses in return. Criss-Cross is a big lad and is still learning his manners; when he’s excited he can occasionally use his size to try and barge past, but he responds well to clear, firm verbal guidance.

He will need a quiet area to enjoy his meals, as this helps him feel more secure. Criss-Cross is doing very well with his harness training and has already ventured out of the rescue for walks, managing a good distance down the road. He can still feel a little unsure if people are walking behind him, and one of his endearing little quirks is that he finds reassurance if you turn and face him while walking backwards. Criss-Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet and gentle giant who will thrive in an active, patient and understanding home.

Criss Cross is a very worried soul who has come to us from a breeder, and is needing extra patience, understanding, and tender care. He appears to have had very little formal handling in his past and can be grumbly or anxious when he feels uncomfortable. He requires slow, careful introductions and time to begin to understand the world around him.

Criss Cross would thrive in an adult-only home with experienced owners who can provide the reassurance and consistency he needs to start building trust. He is still learning the basics of house training and walking on a lead, so his adopters will need to be patient and gentle as he gradually discovers confidence. He will need an understanding and kind resident dog in the home he can look to as he continues to learn and trust.

This sweet, sensitive boy is not yet ready for the full bustle of the world, but with time, quiet encouragement, and safe garden sniffing adventures, he will slowly open up and reveal the loyal companion he can be. Criss Cross will need a calm, loving home where his cautious nature is respected and nurtured and where he can finally feel safe and truly belong.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Cuba
description:
I will need a loving and understanding adult-only home!

I'd prefer to be the only dog. I can't live with cats.

I am still unsure about the world, so a secure garden would be ideal.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked, especially by traffic!

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home. Read below for more!

Cuba is a very sensitive and shy boy who is still finding the world quite overwhelming, but who is making lovely progress as his confidence slowly grows. Cuba arrived with very little life experience and can be easily worried by new situations, so he needs a calm, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust.

As he gets to know people, Cuba is becoming increasingly sociable. He may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he trusts you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy quiet, gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby and finds calm strokes very reassuring, often drifting off to sleep while being gently fussed. Recently, he has started to open up his trust circle and has accepted a few new recruits. This is a big step for a worried boy like, Cuba and we are so proud of him! As his confidence grows, his playful side is beginning to shine. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, giving kisses, and will happily bounce around like a lunatic when he’s feeling safe and excited.

Cuba has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to him. He will need experienced, adult-only adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. Patient guidance will be needed as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a harness and lead. He has recently started harness training and is beginning to enjoy it, but this will still need to be continued slowly and positively, starting with gentle practice in the garden. Once out and about, Cuba enjoys taking in the world at his own pace and loves sniffing everything in sight on his walks but he can be spooked by traffic.

Cuba would prefer to be the only dog in the home, so his adopters will need to be around enough to keep him company and provide reassurance as he settles. However, his kennel mummy has been working with him lately regarding his socialization skills and he is being an amazing boy. He has greeted friends fine, but this will continue to take time and lots of trust. He will need to be the only dog in the home, but these steps show how much is confidence is growing.

He will need a home without cats or small furries as he does have a prey drive.

He is quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character. Beneath his worried exterior, Cuba is a sweet, gentle boy who has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff and is learning that not all people are bad.

Cuba will need a calm and understanding home where his boundaries are respected and he can have his own safe space. With kindness, patience, and the right support, he has the potential to continue blossoming into a truly rewarding companion.

Cuba has had a bilateral entropion repair and has been treated for an ear infection.

Cubawill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

The past couple of weeks I’ve focused on socialising Cuba with other dogs. So far we’ve done a couple of walks with a Poodle Cross and also a Samoyed Cross, and I was honestly so proud of how well he behaved. He had sniffs of them both, let them sniff him, and walked with them close by. He was a lot more comfortable with the Poodle as she was more laid back and not as interested in him, whereas the Samoyed was a bit more curious about him so wanted to sniff him a lot more. He wasn’t overly keen on this, but he didn’t show any aggression whatsoever! I’m going to keep doing walks like this over the next few weeks, and play it by ear.Cuba has also opened up his circle of trusted people at the rescue, and we’re now up to 4!! By this I mean he’s comfortable around them and lets them give him lots of fusses, which is pretty huge for a boy like Cuba with such big trust issues! He’s also been very good at taking treats off lots of other staff members, and will now stop in his tracks when he sees the particular people who usually have a tasty snack for him. Very cute (and funny)!!

Cuba has had quite a busy few weeks at the rescue and has had to put his big boy pants on!! I’ve started taking him into our on site cabin which is similar to being in a home environment. It’s got a sofa, bed, TV etc … so I thought it would be a good idea to start taking him in there to help desensitise him to new things.

Obviously he’s never been in a home before, so everything was completely brand new for him. The first time he was very nervous and really didn’t know what to do at all. He was holding himself low to the floor and hunched, but he was walking around doing little sniffs of things. I was sat on the sofa and he did come over to me a couple of times for reassurance which did help a little, but after about only 5 minutes I took him back to his kennel as I didn’t want to overdo it.

The second time he was still nervous again, but after a little while he did start to drop his guard and became quite curious. He kept coming over to me for a fuss and a treat, so that was a really good sign being brave enough to eat in there. He was fascinated by the TV and didn’t quite know what to think of it. He was a bit scared of it I think, but equally as intrigued. I’m going to keep taking him into the cabin once a week or so just to ease him into it slowly, and then hopefully that will help his transition to home life when he does get adopted.

Cuba has been with me for over 3 months now and I literally love him more and more every day. I’m lucky to have a very close relationship with him and he loves me and trusts me completely, so I see a side to him that not many other people get to see.

He absolutely oozes charisma and character, and he makes me laugh and smile every time we’re together. He’s fiercely loyal, super affectionate, and SO comical. He gives the best of everything. He loves running around the yard with me and playing with toys, but loves a big sit down snuggle equally as much. So much so, he now likes to sprawl across my whole lap and fall into a deep sleep on me (snores and all)! His kennel is filled with plush toys that he loves to carry around in his mouth and sleep with, and he’s SO gentle with them. Isn’t he just the sweetest boy!?

He does still find a lot of things quite challenging, but I do feel as though we’re still making steady progress, and you can’t rush certain things. He’s still very easily spooked by loud noises, cars passing, people trying to approach him etc, so on walks especially I do have to make sure I’m paying complete attention to him. Most of the time he does recover quickly with a bit of reassurance from me, but then sometimes it will ruin his whole walk and he’ll immediately want to turn around and go back to the safety of his kennel. That’s okay though - I always allow it and take him back to make sure he knows he always has a safe place as and when he needs it.

We’ve briefly mentioned in a previous update that Cuba doesn’t like other dogs that much, but I hope this won’t put you off him as he’s not reactive to other dogs out on walks or anything like that - he simply just doesn’t like to share his space with them. I don’t think he was socialised with others apart from his old kennel friend before he came to us, so I think it’s understandable.

If you have the time and the patience to put the work in with Cuba, I can promise you 10 times over that adopting him will be the best decision of your life. Once he settles, he will truly be your best friend and the love of your life. That’s how I feel about him and I’m just his kennel mum!! He is utterly special and he deserves someone equally as special, who will love him as much as he will love them. He has such a big heart and he really does deserve the world and more.

Cuba has come on leaps and bounds over the past few weeks, and I feel so lucky to have been appointed as his “Kennel Auntie,” spending two days a week with this incredibly handsome boy.

Although Cuba can still be wary of strangers, the bond he forms once he trusts you is truly something special. Knowing him from when he first arrived, you honestly wouldn’t recognise him now. He used to hide away at the back of his kennel, wishing we would go away, now he demands to be the centre of attention and absolutely smothers you in kisses. While he may take a little time to warm up to new people, once he feels safe, his affectionate nature shines through.

Cuba has taken some big steps (quite literally!) and is absolutely smashing his harness training. His progress has been incredible, and his confidence grows more each day. He happily trots along on walks, tail wagging, taking in all the exciting new smells he’s never experienced before. Watching him discover so many “firsts” is truly magical.

We’ve found that Cuba isn’t too fussed about other dogs (aside from his kennel friend Chippy), so he would be best suited to a home where he can be the only dog. This will allow him to soak up all the love and attention he thrives on.

I cherish every moment I get to spend with Cuba. He is the sweetest, soppiest boy. He is so full of love, yet not enough people get to see this side of him. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, bouncing around like a lunatic, giving kisses, and sniffing everything in sight on his walks. But most of all, he loves his people.

There isn’t a moment with Cuba where you won’t feel loved. He makes every second count and whoever is lucky enough to adopt him should do the same. He truly is a special boy, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on him.

Cuba has been on my section for a few weeks now and I am just head over heels in love with him. I knew he was a nervous and sensitive boy so I have taken things slow with him and left him be to suss me out and get used to my routine, but it really didn’t take long for him to become quite attached to me. Within a few days he started to trust me, and now I would say he actually trusts me completely. So much so, I’ve been able to start harness training with him, put medication in his eyes after his surgery, and he’s given me his belly a couple of times for fusses!!!

I still haven’t taken him outside of the secure yard on his harness yet, but I do think he’s ready so I’m going to try it really soon. His biggest fear was having any tension on the lead - he would get really spooked by it and panic - but I think we’re just about over that now and he’s gotten used to it.With Cuba, once he gets to know you and forms a bond with you he is an extremely affectionate, happy, and playful boy, but he is still standoffish with people he doesn’t know and he doesn’t trust them to touch him or handle him. This is something his future adopters will need to take into consideration and prepare for. He’ll just need to be given some time, patience and gentleness to begin with. I am certain he’ll come around, but it will need to be in his own time as he can’t be pushed.

Cuba is hilarious and so goofy, and he will make such a great addition to someone’s home in time, but it does need to be the right home to ensure he’s set up for only success. I adore him very much and I just know his future parents will too, so please keep him in mind if you think you could be a good match for him!

Cuba is making lovely progress and is becoming increasingly sociable as his confidence grows. He is still finding walking on a harness quite scary and will need a patient home willing to help him continue this training at his own pace.

Cuba may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he knows you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy a gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby, quietly enjoying being stroked as he drifts off to sleep.

At heart, he is a very sweet and gentle boy who is learning to trust and has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff. He is simply a scared boy who needs a fresh start in a calm, understanding and respectful home where he can continue to blossom.

Cuba is a very nervous and shy boy who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. He needs a slow, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust, but once he feels safe with someone, he will allow calm, gentle fuss while settled in his bed, which he finds very reassuring. Underneath his worried exterior, Cuba is simply a big, scared baby who needs kindness, patience, and understanding to help him feel secure.

Cuba will need an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be completely new to him. His adopters will need to be patient and supportive as he learns about home life, including house training and how to walk on a harness and lead. Gentle practice in the garden will be an important starting point before he is ready to venture further afield.

Cuba will also need at least one kind, confident resident dog in the home. He gains comfort and confidence from other dogs and will benefit greatly from having a calm canine role model to help guide him and show him that the world is a safe place. He is not suitable to be an only dog.

Cuba is currently learning to walk on a harness, but this is something he finds very challenging and will require a great deal of time, patience, and dedication. He is also quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character.

Cuba will need a calm, quiet home where he can have his own safe space and plenty of downtime alongside gentle interaction. With love, reassurance, and understanding adopters, he will slowly begin to realise that not all people are bad and that he is finally safe. In the right home, with the right support, Cuba has the potential to blossom into a deeply rewarding companion.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Mischu
description:
Mischu is an 11 year old male Cross-Breed. He must live in a dog and pet-free home. Mischu came to us with his sister Iza after spending 8 years in a shelter with very little human socialization.

When they came to us they were very scared and shy dogs. He is very bonded with his sister but isn’t keen on other dogs so if they are rehomed separately he needs to be in a pet and dog-free home.

When they arrived they were both very scared of everything, but over time have relaxed into life here and become firm favorites with our volunteers.

Mischu is the most confident of the two, but his little sister Iza definitely wears the pants in their relationship.

Mischu loves doing the zoomies, snoozing, food, and a cuddle.

He will need work on lead training so his family will need a secure home and garden to begin his training.

If you can offer him, love, comfort and patience we would really like to hear from you.

name: Bentley
description:
Meet Bentley – the gentle boy with a heart full of love! Bentley is a handsome and lovable large/medium boy who is looking for his forever home.

Bentley is a five month old male Cross-Breed. He may be a big boy in size, but his heart is even bigger! Bentley’s journey has not been an easy one. Rescued as a puppy, he spent his early years in a Romanian vet clinic after being diagnosed with diabetes.

Despite his condition, Bentley remained a sweet and affectionate pup, but sadly, no rescues offered to take him on due to the ongoing medical costs. That’s when we stepped in and brought him to the UK in June 2024, giving him the second chance he truly deserves.

Since arriving in the UK, Bentley has flourished! With regular vet visits and medication, his diabetes is now stable. He is such a trooper and takes his daily medications and regular blood tests in stride.

Bentley is the most patient, gentle, and loving dog you’ll ever meet, and his calm, positive nature makes him a joy to be around.

Bentley’s diabetes does require him to follow a strict diet to keep his glucose levels stable. His adoptive family will need to commit to maintaining this routine, but Bentley’s loving nature and wonderful personality make it all worthwhile.

He gets along beautifully with other dogs and has also lived alongside cats in the vets, so he’d be happy in a multi-pet household. His favourite things include sunbathing, cuddling with his human friends, and being the centre of attention (he’s quite the charmer!).

Bentley has won the hearts of everyone who meets him, and it’s impossible not to smile when you see his sweet face. Despite his remarkable qualities, Bentley has had little interest from potential adopters. We believe this is largely due to his ongoing medical condition even though he rarely needs to see a vet now that his condition is well under control.

As a charity, we are committed to continuing Bentley’s insulin medication costs for as long as necessary, but what he truly needs now is a family who will appreciate his kind spirit and give him the love he deserves.

Please note that Bentley would thrive in an adult-only home where he can live safely with his strict diet and no temptation for food outside of his prescribed meals.

We know Bentley has so much love to give, and with your help, he’ll find the perfect home where he can live the rest of his days surrounded by warmth, love, and cuddles. Thank you for considering giving this incredible boy the life he deserves!

name: Lana
description:
Lana is a stunning 2 year old female crossbreed who needs a new home of her own through no fault of her own.

She was originally saved from being beaten on the streets in Uzbekistan as a puppy and they thought from her markings she was a Jack Russell.

However she is now 30kg and was far too large for the couple who saved her (who are in their 80s) to cope with. Their daughter brought her to the UK but lives in an apartment with no outdoor space and Lana simply doesn’t cope with city centre living and no garden.

She’s a wonderful girl and happily met me at her assessment, had a sniff, licked my hand and trotted beside me. We are told she can be barky with some strangers, more so men but she was great yesterday.

She lives with a male dog and until six months ago lived with cats so a home with another dog or with cats would be considered. She goes to daycare and is fine there but can sometimes be too OTT with some dogs if she doesn’t know them.

We’ve no idea what mix she is but think there may be some hound in there as she can be vocal. She walks pretty well and is very food motivated which helps with training.

She’s not been around children so a home with respectful teenagers or adult only is needed. She is vaccinated, speyed and chipped.

Forever homes can be anywhere within the UK but you will need to travel to meet her in Warwickshire.

As always we require everyone in the family and any children who are regularly going to be in contact with the dog to attend the meet. Our usual process is that you will need to come and meet the dog and that adoption is then done on a second meet. For some dogs additional meets may be required and potential adopters will be required to travel to the dogs location for all meets.

If you are suited we will then arrange a homecheck, vet reference and meet with the dog.

We only rehome where all resident and previous animals are/were regularly vaccinated and neutered/speyed unless on veterinary advice. All of our dogs have rescue back up.

name: Bess
description:
Bess is a six year old medium sized female crossbreed looking for an active home. Sadly her owner passed away and she’s not getting on with one of the other dogs she’s now living with.

She is great with children 2 upwards and we would happily rehome her with children of that age. She is a no to cats/small furries and initially at least would be better suited as an only dog. When she was assessed yesterday she was a delight- happy for cuddles and fuss, quickly making friends.

She’s a lively, energetic dog who certainly behaves much younger than 6!

She is fine out and about walking past other dogs and would make an ideal companion for someone who is active and wants a walking buddy. She does pull a bit on the lead but we’d expect that to improve when she’s getting more exercise.

She’s not keen on travelling in the car but can cope with it when necessary.

She is looking for a home with experience of dogs as she does draw confidence from her handler and can be a little anxious at times. She is fine to be left for a few hours at a time but has been known to empty the bin if left for longer!

She’s speyed and chipped but her vaccinations have lapsed (these will be done as part of the adoption process). Forever homes can be anywhere within the UK but you will need to travel to meet her in South Yorkshire.

As always we require everyone in the family and any children who are regularly going to be in contact with the dog to attend the meet.

Our usual process is that you will need to come and meet the dog and that adoption is then done on a second meet.

For some dogs additional meets may be required and potential adopters will be required to travel to the dogs location for all meets.

If you are suited we will then arrange a homecheck, vet reference and meet with the dog.

We only rehome where all resident and previous animals are/were regularly vaccinated and neutered/speyed unless on veterinary advice. All of our dogs have rescue back up.

name: Goran
description:
Gorgeous Goran is a sweet boy who bonds deeply. It really doesn’t take long to make friends with him and once he knows you, you will have a companion for life.

He’s super affectionate and loves cuddles and belly rubs!

He is a medium sized dog, just the right size to share a sofa with. Goran will happily Netflix and chill with you as often as you like.

You can also leave him on his own for reasonable periods, and he is clean in the home and knows only to play with his toys.

Goran is a sensitive soul who can be worried by strangers and unknown dogs so we are looking for an experienced owner to gently build his confidence. Em has been taking him on walks to the park and he has done so well.

Goran could live with cats but would like to be the only dog.

He will be happiest in a quiet, adult only home. He is fine sharing his love between two people.

name: Heidi
description:
Heidi, a 5 year old female Schipperke Cross, can be a worried girl initially but it does not take her long to make friends and once she knows you she is such an affectionate little girl.

She will give you the most wonderful welcome, cuddling into you and rolling onto her back for tummy rubs.

In the home Heidi is clean and non-destructive and can be left alone for a couple of hours. She enjoys her walks and going on adventures. She will make the most loyal, devoted companion.

Heidi can be anxious at times and would benefit from an experienced owner.

She will need a one person household as she can be protective of her owner and guard them from others in the home.

A quiet, adult only home would suit her best without many visitors and no visiting children.

Heidi mixes well with other dogs but prefers her own space so we are looking for a home where she can be the only dog, she cannot live with cats.

name: Elton
description:
Elton is a fantastic 8 year old male Cross-Breed dog, who is extremely affectionate and loving.It does take some time to earn his trust, but he’s very food motivated so after a few sensible introductions he will accept you as his best friend.

Once Elton knows you he is incredibly loyal and will give you the most amazing welcome!

He is a playful, entertaining boy who really thrives off human company.

He will sit and give you ‘paws up’ and loves nothing more than playing with toys.

Walks are also another firm favourite of his.

Elton is selective with other dogs, although he has a group of friends here that he lives with he can display reactivity to some, particularly if he is on a lead as he feels trapped and panics.

We are working hard to help him cope with this but believe he will make the most progress in a calm environment with an experienced owner. Elton mixes better with female dogs and may be able to live with a compatible dog but he cannot live with cats.

He is a bright boy who is keen to learn and muzzle trained, so steps can be put in place to keep him safe during training.

We are looking for a home with experience with handling reactive dogs.

Elton will require an adult only home and care will need to be taken with visitors, a calm and quiet environment is essential.

We all adore Elton here and know he has so much potential in the right home which we are so desperate to find for him.

Short/long term foster homes will also be considered.

name: Ozzy
description:
Ozzy is a fantastic dog who is goofy, lovable, playful and loyal.

His favourite things are toys and cuddles – he’s also a real water baby!

Ozzy is a sensitive soul who can be nervous around new people so needs a gentle approach but as soon as he has spent some time figuring you out he will be your best friend and will give you his whole heart once he trusts you.

He is a bright boy who loves food which makes a great tool for training and providing enrichment. He’s very clever, knows exactly what you expect of him and is eager to please. He’s a real happy go lucky boy who is affectionate and loving.

We are looking for an experienced owner for Ozzy, he needs a safe and comfortable home with minimal visitors in a quiet environment. He is crate and muzzled trained which makes it easy to manage him if visitors do need to come to the home.

We would like to find Ozzy an adult only home, ideally with another confident dog who he can learn from as he loves to run and play with other dogs but he has requested a cat free home!

Ozzy needs someone who has the patience and is willing to put in the time to build up on his impulse control. He is easily excitable so needs to learn some boundaries but he’s really good at this. He’s a young boy with so much potential and will be a great dog for the right person.

name: Axel
description:
Axel is a 3 year old male Mastiff in need of a new home due to a change in circumstances and his family feel they can no longer meet his needs (any negative comments about this will be deleted).

Axel currently lives with children who he has lived with since being a puppy but due to him not being socialised with people or other dogs for quite some time he has begun reacting to strangers so we feel a calm, sensible, experienced adult only home would be best for him.

We are confident that with time and sensible introductions he would be happy around children as he’s very loving and playful with the ones he knows and trusts. He also needs to be an only pet for now, but again this is something that could change in time.

Axel travels well in the car, is great at the vets, and loves a run around a field with his ball. We are going to spend some more time with Axel to get to know him better and hope we can find the perfect home for this handsome boy.

He is vaccinated and chipped, and his neutering will be discussed with our vet. Forever homes can be anywhere within the UK but you will need to travel to where he is in South Yorkshire. As always we require everyone in the family and any children who are regularly going to be in contact with the dog to attend the meet.

Our usual process is that you will need to come and meet the dog and that adoption is then done on a second meet. For some dogs additional meets may be required and potential adopters will be required to travel to the dogs location for all meets.

If you are suited we will then arrange a homecheck, vet reference and meet with the dog. We only rehome where all resident and previous animals are/were regularly vaccinated and neutered/speyed unless on veterinary advice. All of our dogs have rescue back up.

name: Pablo
description:
Pablo is a 3-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-to-large-sized dog who has made incredible progress since arriving in care. Initially, Pablo was a confused adolescent who struggled with communication, often becoming frustrated and overstimulated. This would lead to him jumping up and mouthing, which, given his size, could be overwhelming. Unfortunately, this behaviour resulted in him making a mistake in his previous home.

With dedicated training and patience, Pablo has transformed into a well-mannered and much more settled dog. His love for food and toys has been an excellent aid in his training, helping him learn positive behaviours. He is now a lovable rogue with so much potential for the right person. However, he still needs an experienced owner who understands bull breeds and can continue his training.

Pablo thrives in a calm and structured environment with clear boundaries and regular stimulation. He will need an adult-only home that is quiet and free from frequent visitors or young children, as a peaceful setting works best for him. His new owner must be patient and committed to providing the guidance he requires.

Although Pablo enjoys the company of other dogs and loves to play, he would be best suited as the only pet in his new home. He cannot live with cats. His adoption fee is £250.

name: Rolo
description:
Rolo is a 2-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized dog with a sweet and affectionate nature, though he takes time to build trust.

Once comfortable, he greets his favourite people with enthusiasm, wagging his tail and showering them with kisses. He loves being stroked and will happily roll over for tummy rubs.

Rolo is particularly wary of men and has shown reactive behaviour towards them. For this reason, a female-only home would be the best fit for him. He is currently thriving in foster, where he enjoys home comforts, zooming around in excitement before settling down for a cosy nap on the sofa.

He loves the company of other dogs and would benefit from living with a confident canine companion to help guide him. He has also passed his cat test with ease, so he could happily live with a cat in his new home.

Rolo is an insecure boy who needs an experienced owner to help him build confidence. He is intelligent and eager to learn, but he requires a quiet, adult-only home with slow, careful introductions to visitors.

He also struggles with separation anxiety, so a home with someone around most of the day is essential. He has been making good progress in foster, and with patience, he will continue to improve.

name: Glen
description:
Loyal Glen is a twelve year old male Collie Cross, currently in a Romanian private shelter and available for adoption or foster.

His dream is to be in a warm UK loving home for the winter, as the harsh Romanian winter will be very hard for an old boy like him.

Glen would thrive in a calm, stable home with confident owners who can be his rock. Once he bonds, he is faithful, loving, and will be your best friend.

Glen is still active for his age, but he would also be just as happy to sit and chill indoors with his new family.

As an only dog or with a calm female dog companion

Secure home where he can relax and feel safe

Neutered, vaccinated & health checkedLifetime RBU (Rescue Backup) from Pennypaws RescueHomecheck required

Could you be the one to give Glen his forever place?

This gorgeous boy is ready to be someone’s friend.

name: Galaxy
description:
Galaxy is a 3 year old female Cross-Breed, medium in build but tall in height with her long elegant legs. Some dogs carry an aura you cannot walk past, and in a cage crowded with six dogs, Galaxy was the one who stopped us.

She was painfully thin, her leg hurt, her whole body trembling — and yet, she glowed. There was something fragile and luminous about her, as if she were already named.

She had been left behind with no chance. But fate changed, and she was freed. Now she is safe, and her true nature blooms. Her eyes hold depth — sorrow, gratitude, and a love that overwhelms.

When she runs out onto the grass, she gallops straight toward you, only to roll over and offer her belly for rubs, her absolute favorite. And when she rests her head against you, it feels like a gift of trust you will never want to lose.

Galaxy has a gentle talent: she soothes the insecure. She bonds with frightened dogs, calming them with her presence. She is wonderful with children, playful yet tender, tall but sleek — a young soul full of promise.

Fully VaccinatedSpayed4D TestedBrucellosis TestedMicrochippedFull RBU

And here she is now — no longer trembling, no longer waiting in the dark. Galaxy runs, smiles, leans in, and asks only for love. She once begged for her life through the bars.

Today, she is ready to give her whole life to someone who chooses her. Perhaps she is waiting for you?

name: Bella
description:
Bella is a 3 year old female Cross-Breed.

She is reactive with new visitors, but she does calm down however is generally quite nervous. She has growled but never bitten. Using a safe space when people enter the home will work well for her.

She does not show any reactivity over food or toys. Once Bella is comfortable with people she is very happy, although a generally quieter home with fewer visitors would be best.

She isn’t reactive or bothered by traffic, or bikes or anything like that. Bella travels well in the car.

Bella currently struggles to be alone, being left for up to an hour but can bark and jump up at the window. She can be distressed upon someone coming home and will need someone who is around much of the time.

Bella is quiet at night, sleeps in her bed in the living room. Comes to wake me when she needs to go out, which is only once a night now. Usually around 7am.

Bella is an affectionate love bug, she is very intelligent, quick and eager to learn. Loves her walks, sniffs her way around everywhere including the house and garden. Started playing with soft toys but got bored of them quickly.

Has quickly figured out a puzzle tray containing treats and enjoys any interactive toys. Loves her licky mat and Kong. Lets you know when she wants to go ‘peepee’ by going to the door and scratching, if you don’t notice she will give a little woof or a tap.

Off the lead in the garden she does zoomies, is fast and has a terrific jump, would be great at something like dog agility.

She is very reactive when anyone approaches my house or next door, barks frantically. Bella has improved over her time in fostering a lot and will need continued work to help her settle.

he has attended training classes and done really well with the training and become friendly with some of the dogs there. She lacks confidence and likes reassurance. She is very nosey and will look out the window for hours. She is a special girl that is very loving when she knows you.

name: Patch
description:
Patch is a 2 year old male Small/Medium Cross-Breed. He is a nervous boy to begin with and can sometimes give out a growl, though this is not aggression but fear.

With a soft approach, plenty of treats, and reassurance, Patch soon begins to trust and show his true gentle nature. A safe space in the home where he can feel comfortable will help him settle in.

Despite his initial nerves, Patch is toilet trained, crate trained, and can be left for up to four hours without issue. He sleeps peacefully overnight on his bed downstairs and has shown no destructive habits.

With patience and kindness, he reveals himself to be a very loving and rewarding companion.

Patch is still learning to feel comfortable on the lead and needs continued training with this. When out walking, he can be jumpy and will sometimes hide behind his person if something unsettles him, needing reassurance to carry on.

Walking alongside another dog helps him feel more confident, and this is why he would benefit from a home with a canine companion.

His foster describes him as a nervous boy with a huge love for food, especially cheese. He spends much of his day napping and continues to improve with training every day.

With the right family, Patch will blossom into the loving, loyal, and happy dog he is meant to be.

name: Honey
description:
Honey is a 5 year old female Medium/Large Cross-Breed. She is already toilet trained and crate trained, which makes life easier for her future family.

She travels well in the car and has no destructive habits, showing she is a well-mannered and adaptable dog.

Although she can initially worry when left alone at night, Honey does settle down and learns to feel comfortable. On walks, she is mostly well behaved but can be a little strong on the lead at times.

She loves going out and about, especially in quieter places, where she feels most relaxed and happy.

Honey can be a little nervous in busy areas, so a calm environment would suit her best. She is far more comfortable with women and would like a female primary carer.

For men in the household, she simply needs a bit of extra time and patience to come round and feel at ease.

She would thrive in a home with another dog, as canine companionship helps her confidence and makes her feel secure. Honey is able to live with cats, which adds to her versatility.

She is also suitable for a home with children over the age of ten, making her a wonderful family companion.

name: Pickle
description:
Pickle is a four year old male Cross-Breed of medium to large size who is highly intelligent, full of energy, and loves both cuddles and playtime.

Pickles hasn’t experienced loads of new people in the home, when there are people such as work men, Pickle has a woof at the door, and then is redirected to his safe space and he goes in there brilliantly.

Although Pickle is nervous and can be reactive towards strangers, he adores people once he gets to know them. He has not bitten nor growled at anyone but he does enjoy a quieter home.

He is described as a very happy boy around people he trusts and is excited when they return to see him, once he knows someone he does not bark.

On walks Pickle wears a collar, harness and lead, he is also muzzle trained for his safety as well as people out and about. This beautiful boy walks well on the lead, he is currently learning to heel and is making good progress with this.

He can be strong for the first 10–20 minutes and then he calms down and is a pleasure to walk.

Pickle is good with other dogs and could share his home with them pending a successful meet and slow and sensible introductions. He can become over-stimulated at times and does need to learn manners and socialisation.

Pickle has previously lived with younger children and struggled with this, therefore, he is looking for an adult only home or with older dog-savvy children that will respect his boundaries, around 16 years plus.

Pickle does show prey drive and therefore cannot share a home with cats or small furries. Pickle is toilet trained and crate trained, he can currently be left alone for up to 4 hours with no issues and sleeps well overnight.

Pickle is a wonderful dog – highly intelligent and full of energy. However, he doesn’t require massive walks or runs, he just as much enjoys chilling with you at home. I think he’d enjoy some sort of agility or scent training for mental stimulation.

His favourite things are squeaky balls and sand pits. He loves a good pamper and will stand for ages for a groom and lets me clip his nails. He loves a good cuddle and will head bop you to get one.

Whilst he does have his quirks there are easy ways around them and as long as time and patience is given to him he will make a fantastic companion.

name: Coley
description:
Coley is a 3year male cross breed located in Spain.

This handsome regal looking young boy is Coley, and he arrived at the pound just as it was losing its Lorca contract but he was one of the lucky dogs they held back in private kennels to stop him going to the kill shelter, where the contract was transferring.

Coley is a medium sized boy with a short tan coat and a black masked face.

He is a bit of a Heinz 57 and he is doing really well at the emergency private kennels. He goes out every day walking with a female dog and can see male dogs the other side of the fence with no signs of aggression.

He is very friendly with people and he likes to get fuss. He does have a lot of energy and will just run around on his own, but on his walks he is very good and walks well. Coley is good around dog savvy children.

Keen to learn and knows some commands already, loves attention and good with female dogs

Living with dogs : Yes to females not sure males

name: Prince
description:
Prince is a 5-year-old male Labrador Cross. He is a medium to large dog with long legs and a short coat, giving him a striking, athletic appearance.

Prince has spent the last four years in the care of 2nd Chance Dogs in Cyprus, patiently waiting for his forever home.

His story began when he grew too big for his previous owner, who would leave him locked on a balcony for long hours each day. Eventually, they made the decision to surrender him to the rescue.

Despite his rough start, Prince remains a fun, bouncy boy who thrives on playtime and staying active for as long as possible.

After such a long time in rescue, Prince would benefit from an understanding adopter who can help him transition back into a home environment.

He has a playful side but also potential to enjoy quieter, more relaxed moments once he feels secure. Prince enjoys meeting new people and has a strong desire for attention, which is why he prefers to be the only dog in the home.

He is intelligent, energetic, and perfectly suited for an active household willing to channel his energy into positive activities.

With the lifetime support offered by 2nd Chance Dogs and guidance from an experienced UK Behaviourist, Prince’s new family will have all the help they need to help him settle and thrive.

name: Truffles
description:
Meet gorgeous Truffles! Now in UK Foster & Ready for His Forever Home!

Handsome Truffles is currently in foster in the Suffolk/Essex border in the UK. He is a small dog, weighing approximately 10kg and 42cm tall. Truffles is gradually settling in and blossoming, and his affectionate and playful nature is already shining through.

Rescued from a municipal pound in Spain with no known history, Truffles is now on a journey to find a forever home where he can continue to build his confidence and flourish.

Truffles is a sociable and gentle boy who enjoys the company of both people and other dogs. He’s playful, friendly, and has been gaining confidence from his foster siblings on walks. While he loves interaction, he also appreciates a little space when it’s mealtime.

Truffles would be happiest in a home with a calm, understanding dog (ideally female) who can show him the ropes and respect his boundaries, although we think that he would also flourish as an only dog, as long as he has lots of canine interaction outside of the home.

Truffles has already started going on short walks with his foster family, growing in confidence thanks to his doggy friends. His gentle, affectionate side is shining through as he continues to settle into home life.

He adapts well to change, and we are confident that with positive guidance and patience, Truffles will thrive in his new home.

In his foster home, Truffles has been showing his affectionate side, enjoying close moments with his foster family. He’s relaxed and happy, and he’s starting to show his playful spirit.

His walks are going well, and he’s learning from his foster dog friendshow to enjoy new experiences with confidence.

Truffles would love an active home with a kind, patient family who can give him the time and space he needs to settle. A calm, friendly resident dog would be ideal to help build his confidence but a solo home with other dogs nearby would also work.

His adopters should understand that Truffles, like all foster dogs, is still adjusting and will benefit from gentle support and guidance.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella. All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised.

Truffles is neutered. Please note that we will advise results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Jerry
description:
Jerry – 3 year old male Cross-Breed was saved from the streets of Romania this winter.

He has been somebody’s pet but was left to roam.

He is now in a foster shelter. His foster mum says that he is a really good boy. He is friendly and walks on a lead. Jerry shares a kennel with two other dogs.

It’s such a shame that he hasn’t got a home of his own. He so deserves one.

Jerry is neutered and fully vaccinated. He has his own pet passport and is microchipped.

Jerry would suit most families with children over 7 or a couple or individual. He would love to go for walks and sniffs. He is a sociable dog.

He would be transported directly to his new adopter and we provide full rescue back up.

name: Cash
description:
Cash is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a gentle dog who gets along well with other dogs, making him a great addition to a multi-dog household. Although he is initially shy around people, with time and patience, he warms up and builds trust.

A calm and understanding owner would be ideal to help him adjust and gain confidence.

Cash has not been tested with cats, so it is unclear how he would react to feline companions. Any potential home with cats should be prepared for slow and supervised introductions to ensure compatibility.

His friendly nature with other dogs suggests he enjoys social interactions, which could help him feel more comfortable in a new home.

He has not had any known interactions with children, so his suitability for a family with young ones is uncertain. A quieter home with adults or older children who understand his initial shyness may be the best environment for him.

Currently, Cash is in foster kennels in Romania, waiting for a family to give him the love and security he deserves. His gentle and reserved personality makes him a great candidate for a patient and understanding adopter who can help him settle into a forever home.

name: Columbo
description:
Columbo – 3 year old male Labrador Retriever

Columbo is a 3 year old male Labrador Retriever and is medium to large in size. He’s the real-deal Lab — playful, loyal, and desperately craving a home where he can finally be the star of the show.

Some dogs survive the worst, and yet somehow, they never stop loving. Columbo is one of those dogs. This beautiful 3-year-old black Labrador was trapped in a kill shelter, forced to fight for space, food, and survival.

In that cruel environment, he had an eye issue too, but he never lost his spirit.

When we saved Columbo in December 2024, so many people were moved by his story. He stole hearts without even trying—a dog who had suffered but still greeted the world with pure love and trust. Columbo visited an eye specialist, he was operated on, but he did not gain his full vision in that eye.

Columbo is a true Labrador—playful, affectionate, and full of life. He adores people and craves human touch, as if trying to make up for all the love he has missed.

He can be a bit pushy for attention, always eager to soak up affection. Because of this, he would do best as the only dog in the home, where he can finally have the love all to himself. This boy has waited too long to be someone’s dog.

He deserves a family that will cherish him, play with him, and remind him that he is safe, loved, and finally home.

Fully vaccinatedNeutered4D testedBrucellosis testedHe had a cherry eye surgery and has partial eyesight due to the attack in the kill shelterMicrochipped

Columbo has fought for survival, and now he is ready to fight for love. He is ready to run, play, and finally belong. Could you be the one to give Columbo the home he has been dreaming of?

name: Alaska
description:
Alaska is a 2 year 6 month old female Cross-Breed, a golden beauty with a personality as radiant as her smile. Rescued on February 17, 2023, she is affectionate, devoted, and happiest when she has her person all to herself.

Alaska is a dog who loves deeply and bonds fiercely. She thrives on one-on-one attention, cuddles, and being the center of her human’s world. She isn’t just a pet—she is a best friend, a loyal companion who will love you with every part of her being.

While Alaska adores her person, she prefers a home without children or other dogs. She is protective of her space and affection and thrives best in a calm, structured environment where she doesn’t have to share the love she craves so much.

She needs someone who understands her strong, independent nature and will give her the stability she deserves.

If you’re looking for a dog who will be completely yours, who will greet you with endless joy, and who will stand by your side through everything, Alaska is the one.

Alaska isn’t looking for just any home—she’s looking for her person, the one who will love her as much as she loves them. If you’ve been searching for a loyal, affectionate, and devoted best friend who will always put you first, Alaska is waiting for you.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a 5-year-old male French Bulldog. He’s currently in foster care after being removed from a tough situation—his previous owner was unwell and Bruce ended up spending most of his days shut out in the garden while carers were inside.

Despite this, he’s maintained a friendly nature and still has that cheeky spark typical of the breed.

He walks really nicely on the lead and is very sociable with other dogs. In fact, he might be too sociable—he’s been a bit obsessive with the other dogs in his current foster home, to the point where one of them is now avoiding him.

Because of this, Bruce really needs a new foster or forever home where he can have more balance and calm, ideally with someone who knows the quirks of French Bulldogs and can help him channel that energy the right way.

Bruce is not yet neutered, though it’s already booked in. Any dogs in his new home would need to be neutered due to his current behaviour.

He’s not a candidate for homes with cats or children, so an adult-only, pet-savvy environment will be best for this chunky little lad.

With the right setup and some patient guidance, Bruce will thrive and bring a lot of love (and probably snorts) into someone’s life.

name: Casper
description:
Casper is a 1-year-old male Husky. He’s currently in foster care in Westbury, Wiltshire, where he’s been settling in over the past few weeks.

While his foster carers had hoped to become his forever family, it’s become clear that Casper is absolutely not cat-friendly, which has made it impossible for him to stay.

Casper came from a pretty rough background—his previous owners would leave him alone for days at a time. Naturally, that kind of neglect left some scars, but this young lad is already showing resilience.

In just a short time, he’s made real progress. He’s learned to take himself off to another room to relax and was even left alone briefly without any issue. That’s a big win for a dog with his history.

What Casper really needs now is a very calm, adult-only home with experienced owners who are home most of the day. He needs a bit of time to trust new people, but once he does, he’s incredibly affectionate, bright, and playful.

He could potentially live with a calm, spayed female dog of similar size, but he won’t tolerate another male dog in the home. With the right people and a peaceful environment, Casper’s going to be someone’s absolute ride-or-die.

name: Noche
description:
Noche came to live in the UK from Oman in October last year but there have been a lot of changes in his life since then, mainly a baby in the family, so it is in Noche’s best interest to look for a more suitable forever home for him.

Noche is a healthy 24kg, neutered, fully vaccinated (vet records available), up to date with deworming/tick/flea treatment, brucellosis tested (negative), & Microchipped dog.

Noche is an extremely loving and loyal dog. He has learned many obedience skills – from simple commands (sit, stay, break, bed, place, spin, middle etc), heel walking, recall and is threshold trained to certain doors in the house.

He is a typical rebellious teenager at the moment, trying his luck! He has medium energy levels so would love a home with a garden. He LOVES the hills and roaming in the Scottish mountains, in both sunshine and snow!

The ideal home would be rural/semi rural with owners who have the time to give to him. He is not used to children so older children only, he has had good interactions with 12+ year old dog savvy children.

He is selective with other dogs when meeting them/ being walked on the leash and is much better with other dogs when off leash.

name: Jack
description:
Jack is 4 years old and weighs just over 14kg, with lovely long legs. He is neutered and fully vaccinated. He is in foster with a dog called Marley, and they love doing zoomies, though Jack also enjoys just chilling by himself.

Jack is originally from Romainia and came to the UK as a puppy, but sadly he was badly let down by his previous family. Since being in foster he has blossomed and he now walks well on his lead and is fine around traffic.

He is enjoying many new experiences, inclusing trips to cafés and the beach. He is polite when meeting new dogs and people. Within the home he is quite happy snoozing.

We are looking for a home with a friendly, well socialised dog of a similar size, or a home with a garden where Jack can chill. He can be an only dog and can be left for several hours.

Jack travels well in the car. He also knows a number of commands such as ‘sit’ and ‘stay’.

We are looking for an adopter who is consistent in their training, using positive reinforcement, and who will introduce Jack to new experiences in a kind and supportive way.

Jack will make a super companion in the right home but because he can be nervous if things in the home get too hectic, we will not rehome him to a home with children or where children visit regularly.

Full Rescue backup and support throughout the adoprion process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Luna
description:
Luna is a 3 year old female Pointer Cross, large and athletic at 32 kg, and absolutely bursting with energy, love, and loyalty.

This gorgeous girl once had a home, but when her owner had to leave the country, she was left behind—confused, heartbroken, and now stuck in a shelter. It’s no place for a dog like Luna, not when she has so much life and affection to give.

Energetic and adventurous — she lives for long walks, runs, and exploring

Affectionate — she loves human company and cuddles

Strong and spirited — she needs confident, experienced handlers who can continue her training

Luna will thrive in an active, outdoorsy home with people who can match her energy and give her the structure, exercise, and love she craves. She’s not just a pet — she’s a loyal, adventurous companion waiting for her second chance.

Please message us if you think you’re the one for her.

And even if you can’t adopt, a simple share could be the key to changing her life.

Let’s get Luna out of the shelter and into the loving home she’s dreaming of.

name: Florica
description:
Florica is a 9 year old male Cross-Breed and is a wise and wonderful senior chap who’s ready for a peaceful and loving forever home.

With his soft eyes and gentle presence, he brings a calm warmth to any room he enters. While he may have a few grey hairs, he has plenty of life, love, and tail wags left to give.

Florica enjoys the simpler things in life: cozy naps, leisurely strolls in quiet areas to build lead confidence, and the company of kind humans. He’s especially fond of sniffing out new scents along his path—it’s his way of exploring the world and enjoying the moment.

Florica is well-mannered, and past the puppy chaos stage. Florica would thrive in a calm household with someone who appreciates the quiet companionship of a senior dog.

He’s great with gentle people and would do well with another calm dog companion.

If you’re looking for a calm, wise companion who’ll adore you with all his heart, Florica might just be your perfect match.

Adoption ready: Yes, Florica has had his blood tests and vaccines and is ready to travel
